text:
maya: Heads-up — deploy-bot flagged a release tag for v2.3.4 but it's just docs + changelog. Should we skip bumping semver or still cut a patch for release notes? cc @chris @dan

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: release candidate v2.3.4 created by maya. CI: ✅ tests, 🔒 pinned deps. Triggered by tag `v2.3.4+build.1`

chris: if it's docs-only we usually skip the formal release and push docs to the docs site, unless comms/legal needs a public release note.

dan: +1. Our current checklist: if there's no code change and the changelog entry is purely docs, avoid cutting a new semver tag. We can still emit a changelog entry in the repo.

sylvia: small nuance — if the PR included dependency pin changes (even patch pins) that touch lockfiles we should treat as a patch release. Pins can affect transitive security.

maya: The confusion was the tag format — someone pushed `v2.3.4+build.1` from CI. deploy-bot treats any tag with build meta as a release candidate. That made it look like a normal patch.

chris: proposal: canonical release tags MUST match regex `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Anything with `+` or metadata is CI artifact only and should not trigger deploy-bot's release flow.

dan: also: docs-only -> no tag. If product/comms explicitly requests a release, ops can cut a patch tag and add a release note. Otherwise we avoid noise.

sylvia: rollback criteria for patch vs docs: for docs-only no rollback. For patches that modify config or deps: rollback if >5% error increase or if e2e fails in production smoke within 5m. (we should add thresholds to runbook)

maya: Agree. For feature flags: if a change is behind a flag and not enabled by default, we don't bump minor. Minor = visible public API/contract change.

chris: tagging etiquette RFC idea: lightweight tags for normal releases (`git tag v2.3.5 && git push origin v2.3.5`), annotated signed tags only for enterprise builds. Deploy-bot will check `git tag -l` pattern.

dan: we should also avoid buildmeta in release tag names. If CI needs a build identifier do `artifact:v2.3.5+ci.1234` in storage, not in git.

maya: Action items: I'll update RELEASE_CONVENTIONS.md to include: 1) docs-only = no semver bump; 2) pinned dep or lockfile change = patch; 3) feature behind off-by-default flag = no minor; 4) release tag pattern = `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` only.

chris: add example snippet to the doc:
```bash
# create lightweight release tag
git tag v2.3.5
git push origin v2.3.5
# enterprise signed tag
git tag -s -m "v2.3.5" v2.3.5 && git push origin v2.3.5
```

sylvia: also include deploy-bot behaviour: it will only pick up tags that match `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Anything else will be treated as CI artifact and ignored. This avoids accidental releases.

manually: quick question — how do we handle backport patches? e.g., we cherry-pick to maintenance branch and tag there?

dan: backports: yes, tag on the maintenance branch using same rule `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and include `cherry-pick: <sha>` in the release body. Deploy-bot supports branch-scoped releases.

maya: I'll open a PR with the doc updates and a small patch to deploy-bot config to ignore buildmeta tags. Expect PR later today. :+1:

chris: :thumbsup: Thanks — this should cut down accidental release noise.
_reserved_for_slack_thread_format_note: Each message is prefixed with the sender's name. The text field is a single continuous string containing the root message and replies in chronological order.
